measurements.note: measured earlier on L40S as part of CUDA Graph capture investigation

findings: C++/AVX2 implementation of the commutator is approximately 24-26x faster than the Python/CuPy GPU eager-mode implementation, confirming the specification's premise that removing the interpreter from the hot path yields a real, measured improvement, not just a theoretical one

AVX-512 (available on this Sapphire Rapids CPU via -march=native) gave no measurable benefit over AVX2-only on a 20x20 matrix; the operation is too small to benefit from wider SIMD registers, and the bottleneck at this scale is loop overhead and memory access pattern, not vector width

p99 latency (4.95-5.10us) is roughly 3x the mean, most likely due to OS scheduler jitter on a non-real-time, non-pinned kernel; CPU affinity pinning and a real-time-patched kernel would be required before p99 figures here can be treated as representative of a production tick-to-trade tail latency
not_yet_done: custom CUDA kernel for the same commutator has not yet been written or measured; this comparison (C++/AVX2 vs custom CUDA kernel) requires a GPU instance and is the next step before deciding which backend the execution plane uses for this component at batch_size=1
no CPU pinning or real-time kernel tuning applied; current p99 figures are not representative of a tuned production deployment
